title: Release audit: `redact()` in `forgel_code/interactive.py` treats the first word after a recogni
summary: After a secret label, detect that the next word is a plain descriptor rather than a value (no digits, mixed case, value punctuation, or quoting) and, when a copula or explicit separator follows it, resolve the value past the descriptor instead of masking the descriptor; alternatively mask conservatively through the whole label-to-value phrase. Add direct tests for forms such as `token value is hunter2`, `password field: hunter2`, and `the credential value: hunter2` asserting the value is absent from both the displayed line and the retained state, and cover the same text arriving as an engine error.
requirements: When a recognized secret label is followed by an ordinary descriptor word and then a value, the client displays the label and the descriptor unchanged and replaces the value with the masking placeholder.

When a sentence begins with a recognized secret label, is followed by an ordinary descriptor word and then a value, the display keeps the label and descriptor and replaces the value with the masking placeholder.
A displayed sentence that carried a credential contains no fragment of that credential after masking.
Text the client retains for a later status display, and text it retains when a background refresh fails, contain no fragment of any credential.

Masking that already worked stays unchanged: a value bound directly to the label, a compound label whose segment names key material, a credential that follows an authorization scheme word (which stays visible), and a label-bearing Russian sentence are all masked as before.
Ordinary prose that mentions a secret word without presenting a value is displayed unchanged, with no placeholder inserted.
The masking placeholder is the one the client already uses, so the corrected output is consistent with output produced for other secret forms.
The behavior holds for sentences in every language the session speaks, including the Russian label stems the client already recognizes.
The existing automated test suite continues to pass.
acceptance: A sentence that names a secret label, an ordinary descriptor and then a credential is displayed with the label and the descriptor visible and the credential replaced by the existing masking placeholder.

A sentence that begins with a secret label, continues with an ordinary descriptor and then a credential is displayed with the label and descriptor visible and the credential replaced by the placeholder.
No character sequence of the credential appears in the displayed text for either of those two shapes.
The status text the client retains, and the failure text it retains when a background refresh fails, contain the placeholder instead of the credential for those shapes.
Sentences that previously masked correctly — direct binding, compound labels, authorization scheme words, Russian label stems — still produce the same masked output as before.
Prose that mentions a secret word without a value is displayed unchanged.
The existing automated test suite passes.

result.summary: Corrected `redact()` so a recognized secret label followed by one or more ordinary descriptor words now shows the label and the descriptors and masks the value. Previously a descriptor word was itself taken for the value (`token [redacted]: hunter2`), so the credential stayed visible on screen and in the text the client keeps. The binding now walks past ordinary descriptor words (via the new `_descriptor_span` helper), and after a copula it skips plain filler words and stops at narrative words, so `token value is hunter2`, `password field is hunter2`, `token value: hunter2` and `токен значение hunter2` all yield `… is [redacted]` / `…: [redacted]`. Prose that only mentions a secret word (`the token is missing`, `password field updated`, `токен значение обновлён`) is still left unchanged, and the previously working forms (direct binding, compound labels, authorization scheme words, Russian stems) produce the same output. Because every display path (`write`, `show_state`, `refresh`) already masks before printing and before storing, the retained status text and the retained background-refresh failure text now carry the placeholder instead of the credential for these shapes. Verified with the new `tests/test_redact_descriptor.py` (forms, Russian, idempotence, no-credential-fragment, unchanged prose, previous forms, retained state and retained idle failure through a real child-process engine) and with the full suite: `python -m pytest -q` → 324 passed, 326 subtests passed.
assumptions: An ordinary descriptor is any plain all-lowercase word that is not one of the client's function or narrative words; a word carrying digits, mixed case or value punctuation is treated as the credential itself.
When several plain words sit between the label and the value, all of them stay visible and the last word of the clause is masked.
After a copula only plain filler words are skipped; a narrative word (`the token is missing`) means the sentence presents no value, so nothing is masked.
The fix belongs to the masking code shared by every display path; the retention paths already store the masked text, so they needed no separate change.
A short entry describing the corrected masking was added to the Unreleased `Fixed` section of the existing changelog.

review.summary: The attributed change replaces the single-word binding after a secret label with a descriptor walker (`_descriptor_span`/`_copula_span`) that keeps ordinary descriptor words and copulas visible while masking the value behind them, reuses the existing `[redacted]` placeholder, stays recursive only in the forward direction (each step strictly advances), and preserves the previously handled separator, quote, authorization-scheme and Russian-stem paths. The new test file covers both reported shapes (label-led and mid-sentence), multiple descriptors, Russian labels, absence of any credential fragment, idempotency, the retained state text and the background-refresh failure text, and re-asserts the previously masked forms (direct binding, compound labels, `Bearer`, Russian) plus prose without a value. The CHANGELOG entry is an English `[Unreleased] / Fixed` bullet that states behavior, and no file outside the task is touched. No test was removed or weakened, and QA reports every acceptance check and the suite passing.

requirements.requirement: FR-1/AC-1: a recognized label followed by an ordinary descriptor and then a value keeps the label and descriptor and masks the value.
requirements.note: `_descriptor_span` walks the descriptor and binds the following value; covered by the added cases such as `token value is hunter2` → `token value is [redacted]`.

requirements.requirement: FR-2/AC-2: a sentence beginning with the label, then a descriptor, then a value keeps the label and descriptor and masks the value.
requirements.note: Sentence-initial forms (`password field is hunter2`, `secret value hunter2`, Russian `токен значение hunter2`) are asserted in the added test file.

requirements.requirement: FR-3/AC-3: no fragment of the credential remains in the displayed text for those shapes.
requirements.note: `test_no_part_of_the_credential_stays_visible` asserts the credential is absent for both shapes, including a trailing word after the value.

requirements.requirement: FR-4/AC-4: the retained status text and the retained background-refresh failure text carry the placeholder instead of the credential.
requirements.note: `DescriptorRetentionTest` drives the real session with stub engines and asserts `last_state` and `idle_failure` contain the placeholder and no credential fragment, and that the output stream is clean.

requirements.requirement: FR-5/AC-5: previously working masking is unchanged (direct binding, compound labels, authorization scheme words, Russian stems).
requirements.note: `test_the_previously_masked_forms_are_unchanged` re-asserts `password=hunter2`, `token:abc123`, `db_password=…`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=…`, `Authorization: Bearer …`, `пароль: …`, `токен …`; the separator, quote and scheme branches are reached before the new descriptor path, so their behavior is preserved.

requirements.requirement: FR-6/AC-6: prose that mentions a secret word without a value is unchanged, with no placeholder inserted.
requirements.note: No-value prose returns None through `_is_narrative`/`_is_prose`; `test_prose_without_a_value_stays_unchanged` covers English and Russian forms and QA's prose check passes.

requirements.requirement: FR-7: the masking placeholder is the one the client already uses.
requirements.note: The change only reuses the existing `REDACTED` constant and even short-circuits on an already present placeholder, so corrected output matches other secret forms.

requirements.requirement: FR-8: the behavior holds for every language the session speaks, including the Russian label stems already recognized.
requirements.note: Russian descriptor cases (`токен значение это hunter2`, `пароль значение: hunter2`) are asserted; other languages pass through the same descriptor walk, and the label vocabulary is deliberately unchanged (non-goal).

requirements.requirement: FR-9/AC-7: the existing automated test suite continues to pass.
requirements.note: QA environment and suite checks passed; no existing test was modified or removed, and the change is additive to the tested forms.

requirements.requirement: Review-only criterion: masked output keeps the surrounding sentence readable and uses the placeholder the client already uses.
requirements.note: Descriptor words, copulas, separators and quotes stay in place and only the value span becomes `[redacted]`; the placeholder is the pre-existing one.

requirements.requirement: The change is coherent, limited to the task, and excludes unrelated, temporary or generated files.
